headline: PLS.AX rockets +9.76% on the ASX today as lithium sentiment surges, while gold hits record highs and oil slumps — a mixed bag for the portfolio.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a cracking session today, jumping nearly 10% to close at $6.52. There's no single news catalyst in today's data, but lithium stocks have been bouncing on renewed optimism about EV demand and battery supply chains. This is the kind of sharp move that can reverse quickly, so worth watching — but great to see some life back in this one.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI had a strong session today, up nearly 3% to $17.41. AI stocks are catching a tailwind from the ongoing US policy debate around AI regulation — uncertainty about rules can actually lift AI company valuations short-term as investors bet on a lighter regulatory touch. There's also fresh coverage asking whether GXAI is the easiest ASX way to play AI, which may be drawing in new buyers.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG had a solid day today, up 1.33% to $76.20. The broad-based ASX rally (the ASX 200 jumped almost 2%) lifted the whole market, and VDHG's diversified mix of global and Australian growth assets rode that wave. A good day for this core holding.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS closed up 1.22% to $519.67 today on the ASX. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, and it's benefiting from last night's solid S&P 500 and NASDAQ gains flowing through into today's ASX pricing. The US market mood remains constructive.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.46% today to $91.32. Emerging markets are quietly ticking along — no major catalyst today, just a gentle lift with the broader global risk-on mood. Still slightly underwater overall, so patience is the play here.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 1.03% today to $8.63, and it's no mystery why — crude oil (WTI) dropped over 3% last night to $84.88 a barrel. Goldman Sachs also quietly cut their 2027 oil price forecasts, which spooked energy investors further. The energy sector is under real pressure right now.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG nudged up 0.45% last night to $358.16 USD. There's some noise about potential AI liability risks ahead of Q2 earnings, but the market shrugged it off for now. Keep an eye on earnings — that'll be the real test.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT was basically flat last night, up just 0.10% to $390.74 USD. LinkedIn launched a new product called BrandWorks targeting $100 million in annualised revenue — small in the context of Microsoft's giant business, but shows the company keeps finding new revenue streams. No major drama, steady as she goes.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO dipped slightly last night, down 0.16% to $211.75 USD. The company laid out an $8 billion revenue ambition riding on GTA VI, but Wall Street's reaction was lukewarm — investors wanted more detail or bigger numbers. GTA VI remains the make-or-break catalyst for this stock.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Pilbara Minerals rockets +9.76%
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals had its best day in a while, jumping nearly 10% to $6.52. You're still slightly underwater overall (-3.26%), but today's move is a big step in the right direction. No single news trigger — this looks like a sector-wide lithium re-rating. If the momentum holds this week, you're close to breakeven. Hold for now, but set a mental stop-loss if it gives back the gains quickly.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Oil slump is a real headwind
watch_today.detail: Crude oil dropped over 3% last night to $84.88/barrel, and Goldman Sachs has quietly slashed their 2027 oil price forecast. FUEL.AX fell 1.03% today and is now barely above water overall (+2%). If oil keeps sliding — and Goldman's revised view suggests it might — this ETF will feel the pain. No need to panic-sell, but worth reviewing your conviction on energy here.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF surging, but still underwater
watch_today.detail: GXAI jumped 2.96% today to $17.41 — one of the better sessions in a while. The US AI policy debate is swirling (Trump's AI order, state-level regulation fights) which is creating short-term excitement around AI stocks. You're still down 8.51% overall on this one, but the direction is improving. Hold and watch — a few more days like today would get you near breakeven.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA VI is everything for this stock
watch_today.detail: Take-Two put out an $8 billion revenue target built around GTA VI, but Wall Street wanted more specifics and the stock barely moved last night (-0.16%). You're still down 8.66% overall. The entire bull case rests on GTA VI delivering — watch for any release date confirmation or pre-order news as the key catalyst.

watch_today.title: Gold hits record highs — $4,238 USD/oz
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 3.63% last night to $4,238/oz — a big move. This usually signals investors are nervous about something (inflation, geopolitics, US policy uncertainty). It's not directly in your portfolio, but it's worth noting as a risk-off signal — when gold spikes like this, other assets can get choppy. Keep an eye on your broader holdings this week.

watch_today.title: RBA interest rate decision — banks are split
watch_today.detail: Australia's big four banks are now divided on where the RBA goes next. One major bank is warning there could still be two more rate hikes ahead — which would push mortgage costs higher and potentially slow consumer spending. This matters for the ASX broadly, and for growth-oriented holdings like VDHG. The next RBA meeting will be closely watched.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a cracking session today, jumping nearly 2% to close at 8,804 points — one of the better days in recent memory. Across the Pacific, last night's US session was also positive, with the S&P 500 up 0.5% and the NASDAQ up 0.31%. The big standout in commodity markets was gold surging 3.63% to a hefty $4,239 USD/oz, while crude oil got belted — dropping 3.23% to $84.88/barrel. The Aussie dollar is essentially unchanged at 70.49 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong local session today — broad-based gains across the market.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's US session was positive, continuing the constructive mood.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech held up last night, though gains were more modest than the broader market.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil got hammered last night — Goldman Sachs also cut their 2027 price forecast.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surged to record highs last night — a classic sign of investor nervousness.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar barely moved — steady at about 70.5 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA interest rate outlook is dominating Australian financial news this weekend, with the big banks publicly disagreeing on where rates are headed. There's no clear consensus — which itself is unusual and a bit unsettling for borrowers and investors alike.

stories.title: Big Four banks split on RBA — one warns two more hikes still coming
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's big four banks are now publicly disagreeing on what the RBA will do with interest rates. At least one major bank is warning that two more rate hikes are still on the table, which would push the cash rate even higher and squeeze mortgage holders further. This is significant because when the banks can't agree, it means the economic data is genuinely unclear — and that uncertainty alone can spook investors. If you have variable-rate debt or growth-heavy investments, this is worth watching closely.

stories.title: Cut, hike or hold: RBA faces 'no-win' interest rate trap
stories.why_it_matters: The Courier Mail describes the RBA as stuck in a 'no-win' trap — if it cuts rates, it risks reigniting inflation; if it hikes, it crushes an already stressed household sector; if it holds, it might be seen as asleep at the wheel. This is the core tension in Australian monetary policy right now. For investors, it means volatility could spike around each RBA meeting as the market tries to guess which way the bank will jump.

ai.summary: The big AI story this weekend is US politics clashing with AI development. Trump has signed an executive order that could change how the major AI companies — OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic — are allowed to release new models. At the same time, some US states are ignoring Trump's attempt to block local AI laws and pushing ahead with their own rules. Europe is watching nervously.

stories.title: Trump's new AI order could change how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has signed an executive order (basically a presidential instruction) that could require AI companies like OpenAI (ChatGPT), Google (Gemini), and Anthropic (Claude) to get some form of government sign-off before launching new AI models. The idea is framed as a national security measure. For investors in GOOG and GXAI.AX, this adds a layer of regulatory uncertainty — slower model releases could slow revenue growth, but it could also entrench the big players who can afford compliance.

stories.title: 'The AI war has begun': France and Europe worried as US blocks Anthropic's latest AI model
stories.why_it_matters: The US has reportedly blocked Anthropic's latest AI model from being released in certain international markets, with France and Europe alarmed and calling it the start of an 'AI war.' The concern in Europe is that US government control over AI exports could leave non-US countries locked out of the most advanced AI tools. For Australian investors, it's a reminder that the AI race isn't just about technology — it's becoming a geopolitical battleground, which creates both risk and opportunity for companies like Google that operate globally.

stories.title: A GOP revolt over AI is taking shape
stories.why_it_matters: Even within Trump's own Republican party, there's growing pushback on his AI executive order. Some GOP members are worried that heavy-handed federal control over AI could stifle innovation and hand an advantage to China. This internal tension means the final shape of US AI regulation is far from settled — which keeps regulatory uncertainty hanging over US tech stocks including GOOG and MSFT.

stories.title: Trump tried to block state AI regulations, but some states are forging ahead
stories.why_it_matters: Trump issued guidance trying to stop US states from making their own AI laws — arguing that a patchwork of 50 different state rules would be a nightmare for tech companies. But states like California are pushing ahead anyway with their own AI safety and transparency rules. For big tech companies like Google and Microsoft, this could mean navigating a complex mix of federal and state rules, adding compliance costs and slowing product launches.

sport.summary: NRL Round 15 is wrapping up with some big results — the Dolphins smashed the Roosters 48-10 in Brisbane, the Rabbitohs belted the Broncos 48-6, and the Wests Tigers beat the Gold Coast Titans 36-28 in what looks like a farewell to Leichhardt Oval. The AFL also had a big weekend with Ryan scoring a fifth major.

stories.title: Luai leads Tigers to epic final Leichhardt win
stories.why_it_matters: Jarome Luai starred as the Wests Tigers beat the Gold Coast Titans 36-28 in what is reportedly the final NRL game ever at historic Leichhardt Oval. The Tigers are having a solid Round 15, and Luai — in his first season at the club — is clearly the heartbeat of their attack. A win Gold Coast fans won't want to think about too much.

stories.title: 'Embarrassing': Warriors coach in rare blow-up after 'most unprofessional thing I've seen'
stories.why_it_matters: The Warriors coach let loose after his side's 10-8 loss to the Sharks at Go Media Stadium, calling something that happened during the game 'the most unprofessional thing I've seen' and labelling the incident 'embarrassing.' The Warriors are one of the form sides of the competition, so any cracks in the camp are worth watching heading into the second half of the season.

stories.title: Dolphins thrash Roosters 48-10 at Suncorp
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins put on a clinic at Suncorp Stadium on Friday night, hammering the Sydney Roosters 48-10. It's a statement win for the Dolphins and a worrying performance from the Roosters, who were completely outclassed. The Dolphins look like genuine finals contenders at this stage of the season.

stories.title: 'Piece of s***': AFL awards outfit storm erupts
stories.why_it_matters: A controversy has erupted around the AFL's annual awards ceremony, with players and commentators slamming the event's outfit standards — one anonymous player reportedly called it a 'piece of s***.' The row appears to centre on dress code rules or presentation choices at the ceremony, and it's blowing up on social media heading into the week. Classic AFL off-field drama.
